## The gap between evaluation and access

The mixed-diabetes audit by [Reinders et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.diabres.2024.111833) covered 21 studies, 23 research-origin games and 13 app-store games:

1. **21 of 23 research-origin games were not publicly available.**
2. No identified web or personal-computer research game could be located; only one of 11 research mobile games was free in Google Play.
3. All 13 app-store games were visible in Apple's store, five in Google Play and 11 were free; these products generally lacked peer-reviewed product-level outcome evaluation.

This is a point-in-time finding, **not a disappearance rate**: it does not establish prior public release or why access was absent. The sample combines type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D), so the proportions are not T1D-specific estimates.

## Finding a usable product

The [catalogue](../../explorer.html) distinguishes public products, uncertain acquisition, study-only interventions, prototypes and discontinued games. Price, language, hardware, account restrictions and verification dates are recorded for each game.

A product page is not necessarily a download route. [Novi-Chek](../../explorer.html#game-novi-chek) retained an official page while its tested store links returned HTTP 404 in September 2026. [FlightGlucose](../../explorer.html#game-flightglucose) had indexed information but failed direct local connections. Neither was counted as verified current public acquisition.

“Free” does not imply account-free, device-independent or globally available. Installation and play were not tested in this desk review. [Why games disappear](../sustainability/why-games-disappear.qmd) examines maintenance and adoption hypotheses separately from these access observations.

## References

[Reinders, E.F.H. et al. (2024) ‘Serious digital games for diabetes mellitus: A scoping review of its current state, accessibility, and functionality for patients and healthcare providers’, *Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice*, 216, 111833.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.diabres.2024.111833)
